1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 4:29. Alternate translation: [Quickly, take]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:20. Alternate translation: [with you]

2.note: It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [to there, and see Jehu, the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:6. Alternate translation: [his fellow soldiers]

The phrase **a chamber in a chamber** describes an inner room within another room, likely referring to the most secluded or private area of a building. If your readers would not be familiar with rooms that have other rooms inside them, you could use a more general term or explain the arrangement in a footnote. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Kings 20:30. Alternate translation: [an inner room]

3.q: וְ⁠אָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥י⁠ךָֽ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
3.note: There are three levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Elisha said to this young prophet (level 1), continuing from the previous verse. This includes what the prophet was supposed to say to Jehu (level 2). That included a quotation from Yahweh (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

3.q: וְ⁠אָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥י⁠ךָֽ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and you shall tell him that Yahweh says that he has anointed him king over Israel]

4.note: As this **young man** becomes the main character in this part of the narrative, the author is introducing him more formally as a participant in the story. The phrase **the young man, the prophet** is probably equivalent to “one of the sons of the prophets” in verse 1. If your language has its own way of introducing new participants, you could use it here in your translation. Alternate translation: [So that certain young man who was one of the sons of the prophets went to Ramoth Gilead]

5.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:9.

6.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מְשַׁחְתִּ֧י⁠ךָֽ לְ⁠מֶ֛לֶךְ אֶל־עַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, the God of Israel, says that he has anointed you as king over his people, over Israel]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person because he is making an authoritative proclamation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my people]

7.q: וְ⁠הִ֨כִּיתָ֔ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית אַחְאָ֖ב אֲדֹנֶ֑י⁠ךָ וְ⁠נִקַּמְתִּ֞י דְּמֵ֣י ׀ עֲבָדַ֣⁠י הַ⁠נְּבִיאִ֗ים וּ⁠דְמֵ֛י כָּל־עַבְדֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מִ⁠יַּ֥ד אִיזָֽבֶל
7.note: If you decided in the previous verse to translate this quotation in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [He says that you are to strike the house of Ahab your master so that he may avenge the blood of his servants the prophets and the blood of all of his servants from the hand of Jezebel]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:23. Alternate translation: [And you shall kill]
See how you translated the similar expression in [8:1](ta:08). Alternate translation: [the family of Ahab here and in the next two verses]

Even though Jehu was now a military commander for Jehoram, the son of Ahab, what Jehu says in 9:25 shows that earlier Jehu had been one of Ahab’s commanders. That is why Yahweh still refers to Ahab as **your master** when speaking to Jehu. Alternate translation: [who was your master]
Here, **blood** represents “death.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the deaths of … and the deaths of]

Yahweh continues to speak of himself in the third person in this authoritative proclamation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my servants]

Yahweh says that this **blood** was **from the hand of Jezebel** to indicate that Jezebel’s actions were the source of the blood. In other words, Jezebel was the one responsible for the deaths of Yahweh’s prophets and loyal worshipers. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [, which Jezebel shed]

8.q: וְ⁠אָבַ֖ד כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וְ⁠הִכְרַתִּ֤י לְ⁠אַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּ⁠קִ֔יר וְ⁠עָצ֥וּר וְ⁠עָז֖וּב בְּ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
8.note: If you decided in the verse 6 to translate this quotation in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [He says that all of the house of Ahab will perish, and he will cut off from Ahab one pissing against a wall, both one restrained and one set free in Israel]

Yahweh is speaking as if, through Jehu, he will actually **cut off** these people, as if they were plants that Jehu would remove from the ground with a sharp tool. He means that he will have Jehu kill them. Alternate translation: [and I will have you kill in Ahab’s family]

Yahweh is referring to the males in Ahab’s household. To emphasize how angry he is at the serious sins of Ahab and his family and what severe punishment they deserve, Yahweh is using a vivid expression that might be considered vulgar in some cultures. If it would not be appropriate for your readers if you reproduced this exact expression, you could use an equivalent one that would reflect Yahweh’s anger. You could also use plain language. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Kings 14:10. Alternate translation: [every single one of the men]

Yahweh is referring to all of Ahab’s male descendants by naming the two main categories of them, **one restrained** (legal slaves) and **one set free** (legal free men). If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all male descendants] or [every male descendant]

The expressions **one restrained** and **one set free** are passive verbal forms. If you decide to represent both expressions in your translation, and if your language would not use such forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [both slaves and free men]

9.q: וְ⁠נָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כְּ⁠בֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וּ⁠כְ⁠בֵ֖ית בַּעְשָׁ֥א בֶן־אֲחִיָּֽה
9.note: If you decided in verse 6 to translate this quotation in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [He says that he will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha, the son of Ahijah]

9.q: וְ⁠נָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כְּ⁠בֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וּ⁠כְ⁠בֵ֖ית בַּעְשָׁ֥א בֶן־אֲחִיָּֽה
9.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the house of Jeroboam** and **the house of Baasha** were completely destroyed, so the **house of Ahab** will be completely destroyed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And I will cause the family of Ahab to be destroyed completely, just like the family of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and the family of Baasha, the son of Ahijah]

10.q: וְ⁠אֶת־אִיזֶ֜בֶל יֹאכְל֧וּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִ֛ים בְּ⁠חֵ֥לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֖אל וְ⁠אֵ֣ין קֹבֵ֑ר
10.note: If you decided in the previous verse to translate this quotation in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [And he says that dogs will eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, so that no one will bury her]

Yahweh assumes that Jehu will know that by **the portion of Jezreel**, he means the plot of land in Jezreel that Naboth owned and used for a vineyard. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the plot of land that belonged to Naboth]

The pronoun **he** refers in each instance to the young prophet, not to Jehu. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the young prophet opened the door, and he fled]

11.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 5:21. Alternate translation: [Is all well]

Jehu is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you know** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize the other commanders’ personal awareness of the character of this prophet and the way he talks. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [You yourselves know]

12.note: The commanders are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [What you have said is a lie]

Jehu is using **Like this and like this** as a common expression of his culture to introduce a summary of what someone said If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Along these lines he spoke to me, saying] or [What he said to me was]

12.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥י⁠ךָֽ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
12.note: There are three levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Jehu said (level 1). Jehu is quoting what the young prophet said to him (level 2). That included a quotation from Yahweh (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

12.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥י⁠ךָֽ לְ⁠מֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there are not quotations within quotations. Alternate translation: [telling me that Yahweh said that he had anointed me as king over Israel]

13.note: The phrase **hurried and took** expresses a single idea. The word **hurried** tells how the other commanders **took** their garments. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [And they hurriedly took, a man his garment]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:23. Alternate translation: [And each man hurriedly took his own garment]

Putting their garments **under** Jehu (that is, letting him stand on them) was a symbolic action by which the commanders showed him honor. They were treating him as a person who was so great that his feet should not touch the ground. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote.

The word that the ULT translates as **top** is an architectural term whose precise meaning is no longer certain. The context suggests, however, that the other commanders wanted to put Jehu in a high location to honor him and make him visible, so most translations understand the term to refer to the top of a staircase. However, some versions translate the term in other ways. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

The act of blowing on a **shofar** was a symbolic action by these commanders showed that they were supporting Jehu as king instead of Jehoram, the son of Ahab. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And they blew on a shofar to show that they were supporting him as king]

14.q: וְ⁠יוֹרָם֩ הָיָ֨ה שֹׁמֵ֜ר בְּ⁠רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֗ד ה֚וּא וְ⁠כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִ⁠פְּנֵ֥י חֲזָאֵ֖ל מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲרָֽם
14.note: In this sentence and the first sentence of the next verse, the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of how the author calls this king both **Joram** and Jehoram. In this chapter, follow the same decision you made in chapter 8 about whether to call him Jehoram consistently or to use the same forms of his name that the author does in each place.
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:6. Alternate translation: [he and the whole Israelite army]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16. Alternate translation: [against the attack by]

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:29. Alternate translation: [to recuperate]
Jehu is using the **soul** of the other commanders, their inner being, to mean their desire. Alternate translation: [If it is your desire]
The word **your** is plural here because Jehu is addressing the other commanders, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Jehu is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [If it is your desire to make me the king]

16.q: וַ⁠יִּרְכַּ֤ב יֵהוּא֙ וַ⁠יֵּ֣לֶךְ יִזְרְעֶ֔אלָ⁠ה כִּ֥י יוֹרָ֖ם שֹׁכֵ֣ב שָׁ֑מָּ⁠ה
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And because Joram was lying down there, Jehu rode and went to Jezreel]

The phrase **rode and went** expresses a single idea. The word **rode**, which indicates that Jehu rode in his chariot, tells in what way he **went** to Jezreel. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [And Jehu went in his chariot]

Here, **lying down** represents “recuperating.” It conveys the further idea that Joram was not in fully fit condition to fight Jehu. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Joram was laid up there] or [Joram was recuperating there]

16.q: וַֽ⁠אֲחַזְיָה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה יָרַ֖ד לִ⁠רְא֥וֹת אֶת־יוֹרָֽם
16.note: The author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
See how you translated the similar expression “go up” in 1:3. Alternate translation: [Now Ahaziah, the king of Judah, had gone]

17.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and have the horseman ask them whether they are coming in peace]

Jehoram is instructing this messenger to leave out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Are you coming in peace]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **word**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Are you coming peacefully]

18.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [The king asks whether you are coming in peace]

Jehu is using **What to you and to peace** as a common expression of his culture to mean that whether he is coming in peace has nothing to do with this messenger. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, here and in the next verse, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What business is it of yours whether I am coming in peace] or [Why should I tell you whether I am coming in peace]

Jehu is using the question form to indicate forcefully that he will not discuss with this messenger whether he is coming in peace. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is none of your business whether I am coming in peace!] or [I do not need to tell you whether I am coming in peace!]

19.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **second**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [another rider on a horse]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. In this case, the rider is making a statement on behalf of the king rather than asking a question. Alternate translation: [The king says he hopes that you are coming in peace]

20.note: The watchman assumes that the king will understand that by **the driving**, he means the driving of the person to whom the two messengers spoke. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the driving of the person to whom the two messengers spoke]
Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. Alternate translation: [I say that because]

The watchman is saying **with madness** as an overstatement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [furiously]

21.note: Joram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Harness my chariot]

The author does not mean that Jehoram and Ahaziah had to look for Jehu and that they **found him** at the location he describes. He means that they met or encountered him there. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And they encountered him]

22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 9:17. Alternate translation: [Are you coming in peace] or [Are you coming peacefully]

22.q: מָ֣ה הַ⁠שָּׁל֔וֹם עַד־זְנוּנֵ֞י אִיזֶ֧בֶל אִמְּ⁠ךָ֛ וּ⁠כְשָׁפֶ֖י⁠הָ הָ⁠רַבִּֽים
22.note: Jehu is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [What peace can there be during the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries?]

22.q: מָ֣ה הַ⁠שָּׁל֔וֹם עַד־זְנוּנֵ֞י אִיזֶ֧בֶל אִמְּ⁠ךָ֛ וּ⁠כְשָׁפֶ֖י⁠הָ הָ⁠רַבִּֽים
22.note: Jehu is using the question form to deny emphatically that there can be peace. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There can be no peace as long as the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries continue!]

Jehu is speaking as if the worship of many idols that Jezebel has been promoting were actually prostitution. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the worship of many idols that Jezebel your mother has promoted]

23.q: וַ⁠יַּהֲפֹ֧ךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם יָדָ֖י⁠ו וַ⁠יָּנֹ֑ס וַ⁠יֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מִרְמָ֥ה אֲחַזְיָֽה
23.note: The author is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. Alternate translation: [And Jehoram said to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!” And he turned his hands and fled]

The author is using Jehoram’s **hands** to represent his control of the chariot. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Jehoram turned his chariot around]

Jehoram is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Jehu is committing treachery against me]

24.note: The author is using **filled his hand with** as a common expression of his culture to mean “picked up.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Jehu took his bow in hand] or [And Jehu picked up his bow]

The implication is that Jehu picked up his bow and used it to shoot an arrow at Jehoram. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And Jehu picked up his bow and shot an arrow at Jehoram]
The implication is that Jehoram **sank down** dead. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he sank down dead]

25.note: Jehu is using this possessive form to describe a **portion** of land that consisted of a **field**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the agricultural property that Naboth the Jezreelite owned]

Jehu is speaking of this divine message as if it had been a **burden**, that is, a heavy load to carry. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [made this pronouncement]

26.q: אִם־לֹ֡א אֶת־דְּמֵ֣י נָבוֹת֩ וְ⁠אֶת־דְּמֵ֨י בָנָ֜י⁠ו רָאִ֤יתִי אֶ֨מֶשׁ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠שִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לְ⁠ךָ֛ בַּ⁠חֶלְקָ֥ה הַ⁠זֹּ֖את נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה
26.note: There are three levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Jehu said to his captain (level 1), continuing from the previous verse. Jehu is quoting what Yahweh said about Ahab through Elijah. (level 2). Within that quotation, Yahweh says that he is declaring something, and he quotes what he is declaring (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

26.q: אִם־לֹ֡א אֶת־דְּמֵ֣י נָבוֹת֩ וְ⁠אֶת־דְּמֵ֨י בָנָ֜י⁠ו רָאִ֤יתִי אֶ֨מֶשׁ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠שִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לְ⁠ךָ֛ בַּ⁠חֶלְקָ֥ה הַ⁠זֹּ֖את נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה
26.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there are not quotations within quotations. Alternate translation: [He said that he was declaring that he had certainly seen the blood of Naboth and his sons the day before and that he would repay Ahab on this portion]

26.q: אִם־לֹ֡א אֶת־דְּמֵ֣י נָבוֹת֩ וְ⁠אֶת־דְּמֵ֨י בָנָ֜י⁠ו רָאִ֤יתִי אֶ֨מֶשׁ֙
26.note: Following the custom of this culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). In a context such as this, it may be natural to express just the first part of the condition as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [I certainly saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday]

26.q: אִם־לֹ֡א אֶת־דְּמֵ֣י נָבוֹת֩ וְ⁠אֶת־דְּמֵ֨י בָנָ֜י⁠ו רָאִ֤יתִי
26.note: Here the **blood** of **Naboth** and **his sons** represents their deaths If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [If I have not witnessed the deaths of Naboth and his sons] or [I have certainly witnessed the deaths of Naboth and his sons]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person because he is making an authoritative proclamation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [I declare … I declare]

27.note: The implied “you” in the imperative **Strike** is plural because Jehu is addressing the soldiers who are with him. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And Jehu’s soldiers shot Ahaziah with arrows at the ascent of Gur]

28.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [with his ancestors]

Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him] or [and he was buried]

29.q: וּ⁠בִ⁠שְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְ⁠יוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן־אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֖ה עַל־יְהוּדָֽה
29.note: The author is repeating details from his introduction of Ahaziah as a participant in the story in 8:25. (He says **the eleventh year of Joram** here, rather than “the twelfth year of Joram” as he does there, simply because at this time people sometimes included partial years in totals and sometimes they did not.) He is using this repetition to signal the end of his account of Ahaziah’s life and reign. Use a natural form in your language for concluding an account with a repetition of some of its details.
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:25. Alternate translation: [And in the eleventh year of Joram]

30.note: The author means that Jezebel painted her eyebrows and eyelashes with a pigment composed of antimony and zinc. This created a dark outline as a setting to her eyes, which made them look larger and brighter. If your readers would not be familiar with the use of this kind of pigment in this way, you could describe a similar cosmetic practice that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and she painted her eyes] or [and she put on eye shadow]

This could mean: (1) that Jezebel arranged her hair in a fashionable way. Alternate translation: [and she did up her hair] or (2) that Jezebel put on a royal crown or tiara. Alternate translation: [and she put on her royal tiara]

31.note: Jezebel is using the question form to challenge Jehu’s apparent expectation that he will rule Israel for the rest of his life after he has killed Ahab’s family. She calls him **Zimri** to remind him that an earlier military commander had murdered the king but only reigned for seven days after that (see 1 Kings 16:8–20). If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for this purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Do not expect that you will reign peacefully after this for any longer than Zimri did, who also murdered the king and took his place!]

32.note: For stylistic reasons, the author is not using a connecting word between **two** and **three**. He may be suggesting that at first two eunuchs looked out, and then a third one did. In other words, he would be portraying Jezebel’s palace staff as slowly but steadily turning against her. It may be more natural in your language to use a connecting word here. Alternate translation: [And two or three eunuchs]

33.note: The author is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it and caused it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. When the author says **he trampled her**, he means that Jehu drove his chariot over Jezebel’s body. Alternate translation: [and he drove his chariot over her body, and some of her blood sprinkled on the wall and on the horses]

The author may be using one person, Jehu (**he**), who was involved in an action to represent many people who were involved. He may mean that Jehu ordered all of his chariot drivers to run over Jezebel’s body If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and Jehu had his chariot drivers trample her]

34.note: Entering the royal palace in Jezreel and eating a meal there was a symbolic action by which Jehu claimed that he was now the king of Israel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And he entered the royal palace and ate and drank there to assert his claim that he was now the king]

34.q: פִּקְדוּ־נָ֞א אֶת־הָ⁠אֲרוּרָ֤ה הַ⁠זֹּאת֙ וְ⁠קִבְר֔וּ⁠הָ כִּ֥י בַת־מֶ֖לֶךְ הִֽיא
34.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since this cursed woman was the daughter of a king, please look after her and bury her]

The expression **cursed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [this woman whom Yahweh has cursed]

35.q: וְ⁠לֹא־מָ֣צְאוּ בָ֗⁠הּ כִּ֧י אִם־הַ⁠גֻּלְגֹּ֛לֶת וְ⁠הָ⁠רַגְלַ֖יִם וְ⁠כַפּ֥וֹת הַ⁠יָּדָֽיִם
35.note: If it would appear in your language that the author was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [but the only parts of her they found were her skull and feet and the palms of her hands]

36.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר בְּ⁠חֵ֣לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֔אל יֹאכְל֥וּ הַ⁠כְּלָבִ֖ים אֶת־בְּשַׂ֥ר אִיזָֽבֶל
36.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [who said that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:7. Alternate translation: [It is the message that Yahweh spoke]
See the discussion in the introduction to 2 Kings of how the author and characters may use the word “hand” to mean “agency.” Alternate translation: [through the agency of his servant Elijah]

37.q: ו⁠הית נִבְלַ֣ת אִיזֶ֗בֶל כְּ⁠דֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּ⁠חֵ֣לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֑אל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֹאמְר֖וּ זֹ֥את אִיזָֽבֶל
37.note: There are three levels of quotation here. The author is quoting what Jehu said (level 1), continuing from the previous verse. Jehu is quoting what Elijah said (level 2), also continuing from the previous verse. That included something that people would say (level 3). Use the appropriate punctuation in your language to mark these levels of quotation. Alternatively, you could translate this so that there are not second-level or third-level quotations.

37.q: ו⁠הית נִבְלַ֣ת אִיזֶ֗בֶל כְּ⁠דֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּ⁠חֵ֣לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֑אל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֹאמְר֖וּ זֹ֥את אִיזָֽבֶל
37.note: If you decided in the previous verse to translate this quotation in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can also translate this verse so that there are not quotations within quotations. Alternate translation: [and that the corpse of Jezebel would be like dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel, so that no one would be able to identify her remains]

37.q: ו⁠הית נִבְלַ֣ת אִיזֶ֗בֶל כְּ⁠דֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֖ה
37.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **dung** that is scattered as manure on a **field** decomposes and blends into the ground so that it becomes unrecognizable, so Jezebel’s body would be unrecognizable. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the corpse of Jezebel will be as unrecognizable as dung that has decomposed into the ground]

Elijah was using the term **face** to mean the surface of this **field**. If this term does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the surface of]

Elijah was using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will be able to say] or [it will not be said]
